draft.title: Vector calculus
card: A position vector r(t) gives where a particle is at time t. Write r(t) = x(t) i + y(t) j, with one component for each direction.
the derivative of position, v(t) = r'(t). Differentiate each component separately and keep the i and j parts.
the derivative of velocity, a(t) = v'(t) = r''(t). Differentiate the velocity components once more.
Example: r(t) = 3t² i + (2t − 1) j. Then v(t) = 6t i + 2 j, and a(t) = 6 i + 0 j. At t = 2, v = 12 i + 2 j.
draft.remember: Differentiate each component of r to get v, and again to get a.

a.q: A particle has position r(t) = 4t³ i + t² j. What is its velocity v(t)?
a.why: Differentiate each component: 4t³ becomes 12t² and t² becomes 2t, so v = 12t² i + 2t j. The option 24t i + 2 j is the acceleration, found by differentiating twice.
a.clue: Differentiate once, and do it to each component.

b.q: A drone has position r(t) = (t³ − 3t) i + 5t² j. What is its acceleration at t = 2?
b.why: v(t) = (3t² − 3) i + 10t j, so a(t) = 6t i + 10 j. At t = 2, a = 12 i + 10 j. The option 9 i + 20 j is the velocity at t = 2, which comes from differentiating only once.
b.clue: Differentiate twice, then substitute t = 2 at the end.

check.summary: No problems found. The card, the example and both answers are correct: v = 12t² i + 2t j, and a(2) = 12 i + 10 j.
